subject: SentryHorizon pilot - tokens/sec model + worst-case headroom request
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya.patel@sentryhorizon.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@sentryhorizon.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request: target TPS & SLOs for 13B model (SentryHorizon)

Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re trying to finalize commit sizing for the pilot so procurement and our infra team can approve the reserved capacity. High level asks:

- Target production SLO: 95th latency <= 350ms for end-to-end generation (avg prompt 120 tokens, avg gen 80 tokens).
- Expected peak concurrency during launch: ~220 concurrent requests for the main endpoint (spiky traffic, 10x burst plan).
- Model: 13B dense / quantized variant (we can fallback to 6B if needed).
- Preferred region: us-west.
- Timeline: pilot starts 2027-07-18, 6-week evaluation.

We attached a short requirements PDF and a mutually agreed action plan (spreadsheet) with expected daily request volumes. Can you provide a tokens/sec and GPU-slab recommendation that meets SLO with at least 30% headroom for sudden bursts? Also include fallback options if we hit noisy neighbors or transient latency spikes.

Thanks —
Anya
Anya Patel
Head of Product Integrations, SentryHorizon
anya.patel@sentryhorizon.com
Attachments: sentryhorizon_pilot_requirements.pdf

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Anya Patel <anya.patel@sentryhorizon.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: target TPS & SLOs for 13B model (SentryHorizon)

Anya —

Appreciate the clear asks and the spreadsheet. I ran a quick model-based estimate and attached the mutual action plan (with an extra tab labeled "tokens-per-second math"). High-level assumptions we used:

- Model baseline: 13B quantized (8-bit) on H100-like instance class. Per-token generation latency (single-stream, median) ~= 2.6ms on our runtime with small batching; 95th token latency multiplier ~= 1.9.
- Request composition: 120 prompt tokens + 80 generated tokens = 200 total tokens per request on average.
- Effective per-request token-time = (prompt tokens are KV-cache warm vs cold assumptions) — assuming 70% cache hit on prompt prefixes during steady state.
- Concurrency mapping: 220 concurrent requests -> approximate active token production parallelism of (220 * 80 generated tokens). But because generation is streaming, we model peak tokens/sec rather than raw QPS.

Summary numbers (steady-state):
- Estimated tokens/sec required at peak steady = 220 requests * (80 gen tokens) / average generation time per-token. With our 2.6ms/token baseline that is ~6,769 tokens/sec.
- To hit SLO at 95th <= 350ms we budget per-request end-to-end: network + decode + model = 350ms. If we assume 70ms network/overhead, that leaves ~280ms for model generation. For 80 tokens, that is 3.5ms per token on average at the 95th. That maps to ~22,857 tokens/sec capacity required to guarantee 95th on pure model time under no batching inefficiency.

Why the big gap between steady tokens/sec (6.8k) and SLO-driven tokens/sec (22.8k): SLO math needs to account for 95th token multiplier, burstiness, and small-batch inefficiency. We apply a safety multiplier of 3.3x to steady-state tokens/sec to cover tail and cold-prefix penalties.

Capacity recommendation (initial pilot):
- Dedicated slab: 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (single slab) to meet SLO with ~35% headroom during typical bursts. This assumes autoscaling + prewarmed KV cache for hot prefixes.
- Canary fallback: 2 x H100 slab reserved with rapid routing to hosted smaller quantized 6B model if slab exhausted.
- Autoscale policy: scale +1 GPU at 70% token/sec utilization, scale -1 at 40% sustained.

Operational notes:
- We can reduce slab size if you commit to a 12-month reserved plan and accept slightly higher percent of requests hitting fallback.
- If you need lower latency headroom (95th <= 250ms) we recommend 8 x H100 to handle larger tails and allow more aggressive batching.

I attached the updated MAPlan spreadsheet (sentryhorizon_pilot_MAPlan.xlsx) with the token math and cost delta table. Ben and Marissa — can you sanity-check the slab count and any workload assumptions (KV hit %, avg gen tokens)?

Next steps suggested:
1) Confirm target SLO target tradeoffs (250ms vs 350ms).
2) Agree on fallback routing policy and canary window.
3) Lock region and commit term for pricing.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Attachments: sentryhorizon_pilot_MAPlan.xlsx

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Anya Patel <anya.patel@sentryhorizon.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: target TPS & SLOs for 13B model (SentryHorizon)

Diego / team —

Quick sanity check and an alternate slab layout that may be cheaper while preserving SLOs under our measured workload patterns:

Assumptions I validated against internal benchmarks:
- 13B quantized at 80 tokens gen -> sustained per-GPU token throughput ~3.8k tokens/sec with opportunistic batching, ~5.2k tokens/sec in high-batch windows (batching efficiency varies with arrival distribution).
- Tail multiplier (95th) measured ~= 2.8x on similar customer traffic patterns when cache warm and small-batch penalties present.

Option A (low-risk): 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (matches Diego) -> estimated sustained capacity 6 * 3.8k = 22.8k tokens/sec; gives ~35-40% headroom for the modeled burst and aligns with the 95th target at 350ms.

Option B (cost-optimized): 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs + aggressive autoscale buffer to add 2 GPUs on 60s scale-up -> baseline sustained 4 * 3.8k = 15.2k tokens/sec, with autoscale peak to 6 GPUs when token/sec crosses threshold. This reduces monthly committed cost but increases complexity/risk for the first 30 days.

Operational controls to recommend to SentryHorizon:
- Prewarm policy: route first 10% of expected sessions through a small warm slab to prefill common prefixes (saves ~8-12% of tail).
- Fast fallback: if end-to-end > 400ms, route to 6B quantized with response prefix "[fast-fallback]"; logs routed to Redwood Console for immediate alerting.
- Canary: 48h canary with slow ramp (5% -> 50% traffic) and automated rollback on latency regressions >15% from baseline.

If SentryHorizon accepts Option B with a 3-month pilot running as-is, we can include 2 emergency spare GPUs for <1% monthly fee. Otherwise go Option A for simplicity.

Marissa — want to add anything on pricing delta line items and SLA notes?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

2) Share the runbook link you’d use during canary (alerts thresholds, who to page, auto-rollback conditions).

If you can send those items by EOD Thursday PST, we’ll aim to sign the pilot order next week and target the 2027-07-18 start.

Appreciate it —
Anya
